sources.title: Console Command List - Valve Developer Community (banid, removeid, say, kick; NO kickid entry)
SourceMod core PlayerManager.cpp - issues 'kickid %d %s' with the numeric userid
Source engine RCON admin command reference - 'banid <minutes> <steamid>', 'kickid <userid>'
Counter-Strike: Source Rcon Commands - banid/removeid/writeid to banned_user.cfg
Admin 101 - shows status output with STEAM_0 uniqueid

notes: Vanilla Source engine commands only - no SourceMod/Mani assumed. Source RCON is TCP on the game port (27015 by default, moved with -port); there is no separate RCON port or enable setting, setting rcon_password in server.cfg is what turns RCON on. banid takes MINUTES FIRST then the Steam2 authid (banid 0 STEAM_0:1:12345678 = permanent): SourceMod core issues exactly 'banid %d %s' followed by 'writeid' and 'removeid %s' followed by 'writeid', and a Source RCON reference independently documents 'banid <minutes> <steamid>' / 'removeid <steamid>'. IMPORTANT: banid/removeid only change the in-memory list - send 'writeid' afterwards or the ban is lost at the next map change; writeid is omitted from the templates because commands here must be a single line. KICK IS OMITTED ON PURPOSE: every source checked keys kickid to the numeric USERID, not the Steam ID - SourceMod's PlayerManager.cpp issues 'kickid %d %s' with userid, totalcsgo documents 'kickid <User ID> <Message>', the Source RCON reference documents 'kickid <userid> "<reason>"', and Valve's Console Command List has no kickid entry at all while describing plain 'kick' as 'Kick a player by slot, userid or name'. No source confirms kickid parsing a Steam2 authid, so kick cannot be templated on {playerId}: read 'status', take the userid captured as accountId, and send 'kickid <userid> <reason>' out of band (or ban then unban). Steam ID is still the right playerId because banid, removeid and cfg/banned_user.cfg are all Steam-ID-based, so a userid would make unban and ban-file reconciliation impossible. status prints the Steam2 form (CS:S emits STEAM_0; the pattern also accepts STEAM_1) - never pass the Steam3 form [U:1:x]. 'say' broadcasts to all players prefixed with 'Console:'. No MOTD command - the MOTD is the cstrike/motd.txt file, so motd is omitted.
